:::{#thm-qp-equality}
#### Minimizing a positive definite quadratic under linear constraints

Let $\matr{S}$ be a $p \times p$ [positive definite](linear-algebra.qmd#def-positive-definite) matrix,
$\matr{A}$ a $p \times m$ matrix with [linearly independent](linear-algebra.qmd#def-linearly-independent) columns,
and $\vecf{b} \in \reals^m$.
Then the $m \times m$ matrix $\matr{M} \eqdef \tp{\matr{A}} \matr{S}^{-1} \matr{A}$ is invertible, and
$f(\vx) = \tfrac{1}{2}\,\tp{\vx} \matr{S} \vx$ has exactly one minimizer
over the $\vx \in \reals^p$ with $\tp{\matr{A}} \vx = \vecf{b}$, namely

$$
\vx^* = \matr{S}^{-1} \matr{A} \matr{M}^{-1} \vecf{b}.
$$

With $\vlagmult^* \eqdef -\matr{M}^{-1} \vecf{b}$,
the pair $(\vx^*, \vlagmult^*)$ solves @eq-kkt,
and the minimum value is $f(\vx^*) = \tfrac{1}{2}\,\tp{\vecf{b}} \matr{M}^{-1} \vecf{b}$.

:::

::: proof

The steps marked "transpose of a product" use the [transpose of a product](linear-algebra.qmd#thm-transpose-product),
and $\matr{S}$ is symmetric because it is [positive definite](linear-algebra.qmd#def-positive-definite).

**$\matr{M}$ is invertible.**
$\matr{S}^{-1}$ exists and is positive definite
([positive definite inverse](linear-algebra.qmd#thm-pd-inverse)),
so $\matr{M} = \tp{\matr{A}} \matr{S}^{-1} \matr{A}$ is positive definite
([operations that preserve definiteness](linear-algebra.qmd#thm-pd-operations), part 1),
and so invertible (positive definite inverse again).
$\matr{S}^{-1}$ and $\matr{M}^{-1}$ are symmetric
([inverse of a symmetric matrix](linear-algebra.qmd#cor-inverse-symmetric)),
because $\matr{S}$ and $\matr{M}$ are.

**$\vx^*$ satisfies the constraint, and the pair solves @eq-kkt.**

$$
\ba
\tp{\matr{A}} \vx^*
&= \tp{\matr{A}} \matr{S}^{-1} \matr{A} \matr{M}^{-1} \vecf{b}
&& \text{(substitute } \vx^* \text{)}
\\
&= \matr{M} \matr{M}^{-1} \vecf{b}
&& \text{(definition of } \matr{M} \text{)}
\\
&= \vecf{b},
&& \text{(} \matr{M} \matr{M}^{-1} = \matr{I}_m \text{)}
\\
\matr{S} \vx^* + \matr{A} \vlagmult^*
&= \matr{S} \matr{S}^{-1} \matr{A} \matr{M}^{-1} \vecf{b} - \matr{A} \matr{M}^{-1} \vecf{b}
&& \text{(substitute } \vx^* \text{ and } \vlagmult^* \text{)}
\\
&= \matr{A} \matr{M}^{-1} \vecf{b} - \matr{A} \matr{M}^{-1} \vecf{b}
&& \text{(} \matr{S} \matr{S}^{-1} = \matr{I}_p \text{)}
\\
&= \vzero_{p \times 1}.
&& \text{(subtract)}
\ea
$$

**$\vx^*$ is the unique minimizer.**
Let $\vx$ satisfy $\tp{\matr{A}} \vx = \vecf{b}$, and let $\vecf{d} \eqdef \vx - \vx^*$,
so $\tp{\matr{A}} \vecf{d} = \tp{\matr{A}} \vx - \tp{\matr{A}} \vx^* = \vecf{b} - \vecf{b} = \vzero_{m \times 1}$
(matrix products distribute; both points satisfy the constraint).
First, the cross term vanishes:

$$
\ba
\tp{\vecf{d}} \matr{S} \vx^*
&= \tp{\vecf{d}} \matr{S} \matr{S}^{-1} \matr{A} \matr{M}^{-1} \vecf{b}
&& \text{(substitute } \vx^* \text{)}
\\
&= \tp{\vecf{d}} \matr{A} \matr{M}^{-1} \vecf{b}
&& \text{(} \matr{S} \matr{S}^{-1} = \matr{I}_p \text{)}
\\
&= \tp{(\tp{\matr{A}} \vecf{d})} \matr{M}^{-1} \vecf{b}
&& \text{(transpose of a product; } \tp{(\tp{\matr{A}})} = \matr{A} \text{)}
\\
&= \tp{\vzero_{m \times 1}} \matr{M}^{-1} \vecf{b}
&& \text{(} \tp{\matr{A}} \vecf{d} = \vzero_{m \times 1} \text{)}
\\
&= 0.
&& \text{(a product with a zero factor is zero)}
\ea
$$

Then

$$
\ba
f(\vx)
&= \tfrac{1}{2}\,\tp{(\vx^* + \vecf{d})} \matr{S} (\vx^* + \vecf{d})
&& \text{(} \vx = \vx^* + \vecf{d} \text{)}
\\
&= \tfrac{1}{2} \paren{\tp{\vx^*{}} + \tp{\vecf{d}}} \matr{S} (\vx^* + \vecf{d})
&& \text{(the transpose of a sum is the sum of the transposes)}
\\
&= \tfrac{1}{2} \paren{\tp{\vx^*{}} \matr{S} \vx^* + \tp{\vx^*{}} \matr{S} \vecf{d} + \tp{\vecf{d}} \matr{S} \vx^* + \tp{\vecf{d}} \matr{S} \vecf{d}}
&& \text{(distribute)}
\\
&= \tfrac{1}{2} \paren{\tp{\vx^*{}} \matr{S} \vx^* + \tp{\vecf{d}} \tp{\matr{S}} \vx^* + \tp{\vecf{d}} \matr{S} \vx^* + \tp{\vecf{d}} \matr{S} \vecf{d}}
&& \text{(} 1 \times 1 \text{: } \tp{\vx^*{}} \matr{S} \vecf{d} = \tp{(\tp{\vx^*{}} \matr{S} \vecf{d})} \text{; transpose of a product)}
\\
&= \tfrac{1}{2} \paren{\tp{\vx^*{}} \matr{S} \vx^* + 2\,\tp{\vecf{d}} \matr{S} \vx^* + \tp{\vecf{d}} \matr{S} \vecf{d}}
&& \text{(} \tp{\matr{S}} = \matr{S} \text{; combine)}
\\
&= \tfrac{1}{2}\,\tp{\vx^*{}} \matr{S} \vx^* + \tp{\vecf{d}} \matr{S} \vx^* + \tfrac{1}{2}\,\tp{\vecf{d}} \matr{S} \vecf{d}
&& \text{(distribute } \tfrac{1}{2} \text{)}
\\
&= f(\vx^*) + \tfrac{1}{2}\,\tp{\vecf{d}} \matr{S} \vecf{d}
&& \text{(the cross term is } 0 \text{)}
\\
&\ge f(\vx^*),
&& \text{(} \matr{S} \text{ is positive definite)}
\ea
$$

with equality only when $\vecf{d} = \vzero_{p \times 1}$, that is, $\vx = \vx^*$.

**The minimum value.**

$$
\ba
f(\vx^*)
&= \tfrac{1}{2}\,\tp{(\matr{S}^{-1} \matr{A} \matr{M}^{-1} \vecf{b})} \matr{S} \matr{S}^{-1} \matr{A} \matr{M}^{-1} \vecf{b}
&& \text{(substitute } \vx^* \text{)}
\\
&= \tfrac{1}{2}\,\tp{\vecf{b}}\,\tp{(\matr{M}^{-1})}\,\tp{\matr{A}}\,\tp{(\matr{S}^{-1})}\,\matr{S} \matr{S}^{-1} \matr{A} \matr{M}^{-1} \vecf{b}
&& \text{(transpose of a product, applied repeatedly)}
\\
&= \tfrac{1}{2}\,\tp{\vecf{b}} \matr{M}^{-1} \tp{\matr{A}} \matr{S}^{-1} \matr{S} \matr{S}^{-1} \matr{A} \matr{M}^{-1} \vecf{b}
&& \text{(} \matr{S}^{-1} \text{ and } \matr{M}^{-1} \text{ are symmetric)}
\\
&= \tfrac{1}{2}\,\tp{\vecf{b}} \matr{M}^{-1} \tp{\matr{A}} \matr{S}^{-1} \matr{A} \matr{M}^{-1} \vecf{b}
&& \text{(} \matr{S}^{-1} \matr{S} = \matr{I}_p \text{)}
\\
&= \tfrac{1}{2}\,\tp{\vecf{b}} \matr{M}^{-1} \matr{M} \matr{M}^{-1} \vecf{b}
&& \text{(definition of } \matr{M} \text{)}
\\
&= \tfrac{1}{2}\,\tp{\vecf{b}} \matr{M}^{-1} \vecf{b}.
&& \text{(} \matr{M}^{-1} \matr{M} = \matr{I}_m \text{)}
\ea
$$

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#exm-qp-equality}
#### The closest point on a line to the origin

Minimize $x_1^2 + x_2^2$ subject to $3 x_1 + 4 x_2 = 5$.
In the form of @thm-qp-equality, $x_1^2 + x_2^2 = \tfrac{1}{2}\,\tp{\vx} (2 \matr{I}_2) \vx$,
so $\matr{S} = 2 \matr{I}_2$, $\matr{A} = \tp{(3, 4)}$ ($p = 2$, $m = 1$) and $\vecf{b} = [5]$.
The hypotheses hold: $2 \matr{I}_2$ is positive definite,
and the single column $\tp{(3, 4)}$ is nonzero, so it is linearly independent.
Also $\matr{S}^{-1} = \tfrac{1}{2} \matr{I}_2$. Then, from the formulas of @thm-qp-equality,

$$
\ba
\matr{M}
&= \tp{\matr{A}}\,\tfrac{1}{2} \matr{I}_2\,\matr{A} \\
&= \tfrac{1}{2}\,(3^2 + 4^2) \\
&= \tfrac{25}{2},
\\
\vx^*
&= \tfrac{1}{2} \matr{I}_2 \sbmat{ 3 \\ 4 } \paren{\tfrac{2}{25}} (5) \\
&= \tfrac{5}{25} \sbmat{ 3 \\ 4 } \\
&= \sbmat{ 0.6 \\ 0.8 },
\\
\vlagmult^*
&= -\paren{\tfrac{2}{25}} (5) \\
&= -0.4,
\\
f(\vx^*)
&= \tfrac{1}{2} (5) \paren{\tfrac{2}{25}} (5) \\
&= 1.
\ea
$$

Checks:

- the constraint: $3 (0.6) + 4 (0.8) = 1.8 + 3.2 = 5$;
- the first block of @eq-kkt: $\matr{S} \vx^* + \matr{A} \vlagmult^* = \tp{(1.2, 1.6)} + \tp{(3, 4)} (-0.4) = \tp{(1.2, 1.6)} - \tp{(1.2, 1.6)} = \vzero_{2 \times 1}$;
- the value: $0.6^2 + 0.8^2 = 0.36 + 0.64 = 1$.

Geometrically, $\vx^*$ is the point of the line nearest the origin, at distance $1$.

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#exm-qp-equality-fails}
#### The hypotheses are needed

- If $\matr{S}$ is not positive definite there may be no minimizer:
  with $\matr{S} = \sbmat{ 1 & 0 \\ 0 & -1 }$ and the constraint $x_1 = 1$
  ($\matr{A} = \tp{(1, 0)}$, $\vecf{b} = [1]$),
  $f(1, x_2) = \tfrac{1}{2} (1 - x_2^2)$ decreases without bound as $x_2$ grows.
- If the columns of $\matr{A}$ are dependent, $\matr{M}$ is not invertible:
  with $\matr{S} = \matr{I}_2$ and $\matr{A} = \sbmat{ 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 }$,
  $\matr{M} = \tp{\matr{A}} \matr{A} = \sbmat{ 2 & 2 \\ 2 & 2 }$,
  whose columns are equal.
  So $\matr{M} \tp{(1, -1)} = \vzero_{2 \times 1}$, and $\matr{M}$ is not invertible
  ([a square matrix is invertible exactly when its null space is zero](linear-algebra.qmd#thm-invertible-rank)).
  The two constraints both read $x_1 + x_2 = b_i$,
  so they have no solution at all when $b_1 \ne b_2$.
  When $b_1 = b_2$ a unique minimizer still exists, $x_1 = x_2 = b_1 / 2$,
  but the formula of @thm-qp-equality cannot produce it.

:::
